provisions_triggered.name: Due Process / Law of the Land

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: Before a State may sever completely and irrevocably the rights of parents in their natural child, the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment requires the State to support its allegations by at least clear and convincing evidence; New York's fair-preponderance standard was unconstitutional.
key_cases.relevance: The federal constitutional floor for the burden of proof at termination, which Iowa Code section 232.117(3) and every Iowa termination decision implement.
key_cases.quote: We hold that such a standard adequately conveys to the factfinder the level of subjective certainty about his factual conclusions necessary to satisfy due process.

key_cases.holding: The court restated and modified the analytical framework for termination to track the text of Iowa Code section 232.116, adopted de novo review for all termination decisions, and affirmed the termination of the father's rights.
key_cases.relevance: The foundational modern Iowa case restructuring termination analysis around the statutory text and fixing de novo review for all termination appeals.
key_cases.quote: The first step in our analysis is to determine if a ground for termination exists under section 232.116(1).

key_cases.holding: On de novo review the court affirmed termination of the mother's rights under Iowa Code section 232.116(1)(d) and (h), articulating the three-step chapter 232 analysis — statutory ground, then the section 232.116(2) best-interest framework, then the section 232.116(3) permissive exceptions — and finding no exception applied.
key_cases.relevance: This is the source decision for the three-step framework and the clear-and-convincing standard that In re M.W. quotes, so a practitioner citing the framework should cite D.W. rather than a later case repeating it.
key_cases.quote: We will uphold an order terminating parental rights if there is clear and convincing evidence of grounds for termination under Iowa Code section 232.116.

key_cases.holding: Reinstating the juvenile court's order terminating both parents' rights to a one-year-old under Iowa Code section 232.116(1)(h), the court found clear and convincing evidence the child could not be safely returned, held termination was in her best interests, and concluded that none of the permissive grounds in section 232.116(3) — including the relative-legal-custody exception in (3)(a) and the closeness-of-relationship exception in (3)(c) — applied.
key_cases.relevance: Supplies what the brief otherwise lacked at step three of the Iowa termination analysis: the Iowa Supreme Court's own application of the section 232.116(3) permissive exceptions, which is where most Iowa termination appeals are actually decided.
key_cases.quote: A finding under subsection 3 allows the court not to terminate.

key_cases.holding: The element that a child has been 'removed from the physical custody' of a parent for twelve of the last eighteen months under Iowa Code section 232.116(1)(e) and (f) requires an actual change from physical custody to lack of physical custody; mere absence of custody does not satisfy it, and the termination was reversed.
key_cases.relevance: Controls the removal-duration element of the most commonly used Iowa termination grounds and requires prior judicial notice of parenting shortcomings before that clock runs.
key_cases.quote: Certainly such absence of physical custody would not provide the necessary predicate for a termination of parental rights under section 232.116(1)(e) and (f).

key_cases.holding: Limiting an incarcerated mother's telephone participation in her termination hearing to her own testimony was error; going forward juvenile courts must let incarcerated parents participate by phone in the entire hearing, and the termination order was reversed and remanded.
key_cases.relevance: The controlling Iowa rule on an incarcerated parent's right to participate in the whole termination hearing, not just to testify.
key_cases.quote: Juvenile judges must give incarcerated parents the opportunity to participate by telephone in the entire hearing.
